summary: Benjamin Cowen hosts Jason Pizzino and Guy from Coin Bureau to preview their upcoming presentations at the Into The Cryptoverse conference in Miami. The discussion centers on long-term macro trends, including the 18-year real estate cycle, shifting interest rate regimes, and broad equity market dynamics. They explore Bitcoin's potential trajectory, weighing the probability of testing lower support levels versus establishing a macro higher low. In the latter half, Guy outlines the emerging machine-to-machine economy, explaining how AI agents will require crypto-native rails like stablecoins to pay content publishers.
tone_evidence: The speakers temper bullish expectations by highlighting structural market weakness, historical multi-year consolidations, and the ongoing vulnerability of altcoins.

key_points.point: Jason Pizzino previews his conference session analyzing the long-term macroeconomic cycle and real estate trends.
Discussion on whether Bitcoin will break below the $57,000 low or find a macro higher low.
Cowen highlights key on-chain benchmarks including the realized price around $54,000 and balanced price near $38,000.
Historical Treasury yield trends suggest interest rates could remain structurally higher for decades, creating a challenging environment for speculative assets.
Guy introduces the concept of the machine-to-machine economy, where AI agents pay websites via micropayments rather than traditional ad impressions.
Stablecoins are identified as the most practical and immediate medium of exchange for global digital commerce and autonomous agents.

predictions: If Bitcoin breaks below $57,000 with conviction, further downside toward $54,000 or lower is likely.
A breakout to the upside could realistically target a range between $90,000 and $150,000 for Bitcoin.
Long-term 10-year Treasury yields could trend upward toward 6.5% over the next several years.
title: Going Live with Ben Cowen - Miami Conference, 20-22 November 2026
author: Jason Pizzino
